title: A zero SDK version can mean its query failed
task_type: Unity Editor asset and build verification
environment: Historical Windows/Unity toolchain only. Current versions and device behavior were not reverified.
goal: Run an Android build with an external SDK and the editor's bundled Java.
approach: Historical failed assumption: The displayed zero and stale generated settings suggested missing or obsolete platform-tools.
what_worked: Historical correction: Choose a compatible tools/JDK pair. In the recorded environment, backed-up newer tools were replaced by the editor's Java-11-compatible tools 6.0; this is not a universal version recommendation. Verification reported by the source: The same sdkmanager failed under editor Java and succeeded under another compatible Java. Corrected queries worked under actual editor Java, and Android Build And Run was recorded successful; a nonfatal XML warning remained.
what_failed: Historical observed failure: The editor reported SDK Platform Tools version 0.0 and failed to list API levels despite installed working platform-tools.
why: Confirmed: command-line tools 20.0 required Java 17 while the tested Unity editor invoked OpenJDK 11; forced execution exposed class-file 61 versus supported 55.
improved_method: Run the failing SDK query with the exact Java/executable/environment used by the build. Separate interrogation failure from actual installed package versions before changing project targets.
when_to_use: Historical Windows/Unity toolchain only. Current versions and device behavior were not reverified.
when_not_to_use: Historical Windows/Unity toolchain only. Current versions and device behavior were not reverified.
known_limitations: This is an independently curated generalization of an earlier recorded failure. No source-side experiment was rerun during this registration; observation_date is the 2026-10-09 knowledge-review date, not the incident date. Applicability and root-cause claims remain limited to the source-reported conditions.
